idea: Train a discriminative domain classifier and select only the top-scoring, deduplicated documents. Steps: (1) Build TF-IDF features (word 1-2 grams, sublinear_tf, min_df=2, max_features ~200k, lowercase=False so WikiText tokens like ' @-@ ', ' , ', ' . ', '= Title =' survive; use token_pattern r'\S+'). (2) Positives = the 200 target_sample docs split into ~1000-char chunks; negatives = a seeded random sample of ~4000 pool docs (truncated to first 3000 chars). Fit LogisticRegression(C=10, class_weight='balanced'). (3) Score every pool doc (first 3000 chars); then do a second self-training round: refit with positives = target chunks + top 1500 scored pool docs, negatives = bottom 6000 scored pool docs, and rescore. (4) Remove exact/near duplicates: keep only the first doc per hash of the whitespace-normalised first 200 chars, and drop docs whose zlib compression ratio is < 0.2 (repetitive junk) or which have < 200 chars. (5) Rank remaining docs by score, count tokens with tiktoken gpt2 (encode_ordinary_batch), and take docs from the top down until the cumulative token count reaches 1.0*T, but stop early if the classifier probability falls below 0.5 (the trainer will then cycle the smaller clean set). (6) Shuffle the selected indices with the CURATE_SEED-seeded RNG and return them.
why: The pool is roughly half spam/code/web/boilerplate, so a classifier trained on the target sample against the pool should fill the entire T-token budget with in-domain WikiText-style articles and no duplicates, where the crude keyword heuristic failed to separate domains.
outcome: dev 2.0002 against 1.9601 for the best at the time, rejected

idea:
Replace the classifier with conservative rule-based tiers, and always return at least 1.05*T tokens so nothing is cycled (experiment 2 may have lost by cycling a small set or by favouring damaged look-alike docs; neither cause was isolated).

1. Features per doc.
   - wiki = text starts with '= ' and the density of WikiText markers (' , ', ' . ', ' @-@ ', ' @,@ ', ' ( ') is at least 1 per 100 chars.
   - rare-word rate = share of the doc's alphabetic lowercase tokens whose pool document frequency is <= 2 and which are not in the target_sample vocabulary. This catches typo and character damage such as 'jzz' or 'Augst'.
   - stopword-bigram rate = share of adjacent word pairs that appear in the target_sample bigram set. This catches word-shuffled text.
   - zlib compression ratio.
   - non-ASCII and mojibake rate (count of 'Ã', 'â€', 'Â').

2. Dedupe. Drop exact duplicates by hash of the whitespace-normalised full text. Drop near duplicates by hash of the first 300 chars.

3. Tiers.
   - Tier A: wiki docs with rare-word rate below the pool wiki median + 2 MAD, bigram rate above the wiki median - 2 MAD, and zlib ratio above 0.25.
   - Tier B: the remaining wiki docs (damaged), sorted by rare-word rate ascending.
   - Tier C: non-wiki docs with zlib ratio above 0.3, no mojibake, no spam or boilerplate patterns ('Click here', 'best price', ' | ' menus), sorted by bigram rate descending.

4. Selection. Count tokens with tiktoken gpt2. Take all of A, then B, then C in that order until the cumulative count reaches 1.05*T. Never stop early.

5. Order. Shuffle the selected indices with the CURATE_SEED-seeded RNG and return them.
why: Clean, undamaged, deduplicated WikiText-format docs should match the target best, and topping up to a full T of unique tokens avoids the cycling and damaged-doc risks that may explain the classifier's loss.
outcome: dev 2.0104 against 1.9601 for the best at the time, rejected

idea:
Damage-only filtering with absolute thresholds and no domain preference, to separate the effect of removing junk from the effect of selecting Wikipedia-like text (experiments 2 and 3 mixed the two and both lost).

Keep a document only if it passes all of these checks:

1. Letter-scramble check. Build V, the set of lowercased alphabetic words in target_sample. For each doc take its alphabetic tokens of length >= 4, lowercased, and compute the share that are in V. Drop the doc if the share is below 0.5 and it has at least 20 such tokens. This catches anagrammed text such as 'aemT uilgiBdn'.

2. Word-shuffle check, on tokens from a whitespace split.
   - (a) Among occurrences of 'the', compute the share whose previous token is one of of, in, to, on, and, at, for, by, from, with, as, that, was, is. Drop the doc if it has at least 10 'the' and the share is below 0.25.
   - (b) Among tokens that are '.' or end in '.' and are not the last token, compute the share whose next token starts with a lowercase letter. Drop the doc if it has at least 8 such cases and the share is above 0.4.
   - (c) Drop the doc if adjacent identical function-word pairs ('the the', 'of of', 'a the', 'the a', 'the of the the') make up more than 0.5% of its tokens.

3. Spam and template check. Drop the doc if any of these holds:
   - len(zlib.compress(text)) / len(text) is below 0.30;
   - it matches, case-insensitively, any of 'click here to order', 'buy now', 'free shipping', 'discount code', 'coupon', 'for sale |', 'limited offer', 'best price';
   - it has fewer than 200 characters.

4. Dedupe. Keep the first doc per hash of the whitespace-normalised full text, and also per hash of the first 300 normalised characters.

Return all surviving indices in an order shuffled by the CURATE_SEED-seeded RNG. Apply no ranking, no wiki priority and no truncation; if the survivors hold fewer than T tokens, let the trainer cycle them.
why: Removing only clearly damaged text (scrambled letters, shuffled words, spam, duplicates) while keeping the natural domain mix should raise the share of useful tokens in the T budget, and it tests whether the earlier losses came from domain narrowing or from damaged look-alike documents.
outcome: dev 1.8909 against 1.9601 for the best at the time, KEPT as the new best

idea:
Keep every filter and the dedupe of the current best exactly as they are, and change only how the survivors fill the T-token budget.

1. Count tokens for each survivor with tiktoken gpt2 (`encode_ordinary_batch`).
2. Mark a survivor as wiki if its text starts with '= ' and it has at least 1 WikiText marker (' , ', ' . ', ' @-@ ', ' @,@ ', ' @.@ ') per 100 characters.
3. Score each non-wiki survivor by the mean log-probability of its lowercased whitespace tokens under an add-one-smoothed unigram model built from target_sample. Use the first 2000 tokens of the doc; higher means closer to the target.
4. Build the selection:
   - Take all wiki survivors.
   - If their tokens are below T, add non-wiki survivors in descending score order until the total reaches T, and drop the rest.
   - If all survivors together are still below T, append a second copy of the wiki survivors (seeded-shuffled) to fill the gap up to T, so the trainer does not cycle the whole list.
   - If the wiki survivors alone exceed T, take a seeded random subset of them up to T.
5. Shuffle the final list with the CURATE_SEED-seeded RNG and return it.

Log the survivor token total, the wiki token total and which branch was taken.
why: The current best fills the budget at random from the survivors, so making sure every clean target-format document is inside the T tokens (and that any shortfall is padded with wiki text rather than off-domain text) tests domain preference on top of the damage filter without the cycling and damaged-look-alike problems that may have sunk experiments 2 and 3.
